introduction-the-staging-bottleneck.core: One shared staging environment serialises testing: teams queue for it, overwrite each other's deployments and debug each other's bugs. Ephemeral environments give every PR its own isolated, short-lived copy.

first_principles.problem: Five teams fight over one staging, tests are polluted by other people's changes, and the queue for staging slows everything.
truths: Automation makes environments cheap to create.

analogy.title: A shared whiteboard vs. personal notebooks
analogy.story: Only one person can write on the whiteboard; everyone can sketch in their own notebook at once.
analogy.breaks: Full copies of complex systems can be expensive, so share heavy dependencies wisely.

example.title: Reviewing a UI change

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: There's no staging queue, and review happens on real deployments.

example.outcome: parallel, isolated testing for every change.

check.q: What problem do ephemeral environments solve?
check.a: Contention and cross-contamination in a single shared staging environment.

lifecycle-management-the-automation-loop.core: Tie the environment's lifecycle to Git events: PR opened → provision, push → update, PR closed or merged → destroy. The PR is the environment's single source of truth.

first_principles.problem: Manually created preview environments get forgotten, drift and are never cleaned up.
truths: Git events mark the start and end of a change.
derivation: Post the **URL and status** back to the PR.

analogy.title: A hotel room tied to a booking
analogy.story: Check-in creates the room assignment, extending the stay updates it, and checkout frees it, all automatically.
analogy.breaks: Missed close events (failed webhooks) leave orphans, so add a sweeper.

example.title: ArgoCD PR generator

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Labelled PRs get environments, and closing removes them.

example.outcome: environments live exactly as long as their PRs.

check.q: Which Git event should trigger teardown?
check.a: The PR being closed or merged.

data-seeding-the-hardest-part.core: Stateless services spin up easily, but tests need realistic data. Seed from fixtures, anonymised production snapshots or copy-on-write database branches, and never copy raw PII into previews.

first_principles.problem: An empty database makes previews useless, while copying production data leaks customer PII.
truths: Copying large data is slow and expensive.
derivation: **Database branching** (Neon, PlanetScale, Aurora clones) for speed.
**Migrations** run on seed data in every environment.

analogy.title: A movie set with props
analogy.story: You need realistic props for a believable scene, but not the actors' real wallets.
analogy.breaks: Anonymisation is hard to get perfect, since quasi-identifiers can re-identify people.

example.title: Seeding with a database branch

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Realistic data in seconds with no PII.

example.outcome: previews are actually useful for testing.

check.q: Why not copy production databases into preview environments?
check.a: They contain sensitive PII, and full copies are slow and expensive.

cost-control-stopping-the-bleeding.core: Ephemeral environments are only cheap if they're actually ephemeral. Enforce TTLs, sweep orphans, scale to zero when idle, share heavy dependencies and right-size resources.

first_principles.problem: Zombie environments from abandoned PRs quietly run for months and inflate the cloud bill.
truths: Not every service needs a dedicated copy.
derivation: **Share** expensive backing services (one DB server, many databases).
Track **cost per environment** and show it on the PR.

analogy.title: Turning off lights in empty rooms
analogy.story: Motion sensors switch off lights automatically, and a nightly guard checks for any left on.
analogy.breaks: Shared dependencies weaken isolation, so balance cost against fidelity.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Nothing lives longer than 7 days without renewal.

code.text:
kubectl get ns -l preview=true -o json \
 | jq -r '.items[] | select((now - (.metadata.creationTimestamp|fromdate)) > 7*86400) | .metadata.name' \
 | xargs -r kubectl delete ns

check.a: A preview environment that keeps running after its PR is gone, costing money for nothing.
